description: Wire Stage 0 (extraction) + Stage 1 (retrieval) into a single prepare_investigation() entry point for the V4 agent pipeline
acceptance_criteria: AC1: retrieval/pipeline.py exports prepare_investigation(jira_issue_or_raw, repo_path, temporal_bound, project) → RetrievalResult
AC2: prepare_investigation uses ProblemExtractor.from_jira_issue() when given JiraIssue, from_raw() when given raw title+description
AC3: prepare_investigation calls retrieve_candidates() with GitContextProvider(repo_path, temporal_bound)
AC4: When CandidateSet has < fallback_recency_threshold candidates, prepare_investigation re-runs with widened RetrievalConfig (2x file_log/keyword/pickaxe limits) — brief-validation retry path
AC5: prepare_investigation returns even if retry still produces few candidates (degraded mode, not error)
AC6: RetrievalResult dataclass wraps (ProblemStatement, CandidateSet, metadata dict with retry_triggered, strategies_used, total_raw)
AC7: Tests cover: normal path, widened-retry path, degraded mode (zero signals), JiraIssue input, raw input
AC8: One end-to-end pytest using real repo (CASSANDRA-7570 via data/repos/cassandra) proving prepare_investigation returns non-empty CandidateSet — marked @pytest.mark.slow
AC9: pipeline.py is exported from retrieval/__init__.py
AC10: All existing 330 tests + new tests pass with zero regressions (actual: 372 pass)
edge_cases: EC1: Repo not found raises GitRepoNotFoundError (not swallowed)
EC3: Empty title + empty description → ProblemStatement.is_empty=True, retrieval falls back to recency
EC4: Real repo test skips if repo not cloned
evaluator_findings: AC1 vs AC6 wording: AC1 originally said tuple, implementation correctly returns RetrievalResult per AC6 (non-blocking)
EC2 has no dedicated unit test (verified via code review + live spot-check)
EC3 recency-fallback path confirmed at runtime but not explicitly asserted in mocked test
